A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Value-Guided Search work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original math-benchmark experiments, search ablations, PPO-policy evaluations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results and additionally reports a training/test overlap check.

M1.justification: The token-level classifier, cross-entropy objective, roll-in/roll-out data pipeline, and block-wise beam search with DVTS and weighted majority voting remain unchanged. Sections 2 and Appendices B, D–G describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenR1-derived training data and evaluate AIME and February HMMT for 2024 and 2025. Although v2 emphasizes the 2025 evaluations, all four competitions remain represented in Appendix C; no dataset or task coverage is removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain the same, including MV, WMV, BoN, Bradley-Terry scoring, Math-Shepherd, and Qwen2.5-Math-PRM. DeepSeek and OpenAI model comparisons omitted from v2's shortened Table 1 remain in Table 2. The newly cited confidence-based method is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes the default evaluation aggregate from all four competitions to AIME-25 and HMMT-25, materially redefining the primary test performance reported in Table 1 and the scaling plots. V2 explicitly identifies AIME-24 as validation data and reports an overlap-control procedure. This establishes a revised reporting protocol, not that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a contamination sanity check reporting no training/test problems with greater than 50% 8-gram overlap. The DVTS and random-search ablation plots are reaggregated over the 2025 benchmarks. The ablation questions, PPO analyses, response-length analysis, and qualitative cases otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report VGS standard deviations across three seeds and bootstrap uncertainty using 100 repetitions for MV, WMV, and Pass@N. Changed uncertainty values accompanying the new averages do not represent a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 introduces two-benchmark averages: at N=256, VGS changes from a four-benchmark 45.7% to 39.8%, WMV from 43.2% to 37.0%, and MV from 39.7% to 31.6%. Corresponding aggregate curves change. These reflect different aggregation, not performance deterioration; Table 2 and the per-benchmark appendix results retain the original values.

T1.justification: The classifier/value definitions, expected-reward interpretation, training losses, PPO expressions, and Appendix H FLOPs derivation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract/introduction claim linking 64-generation DeepSeek-1.5B search to o3-mini-medium performance, including the abstract's 45.7% figure. The existing 256-generation comparison remains in Appendix C.1. The central method, efficiency, and test-time-scaling contributions are retained.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's general concern about unusually strong AIME-24 results with an explicit temporal-contamination rationale for emphasizing the 2025 tests. Appendix A also discusses the training-free advantage and possible long-term planning limitations of confidence-based guidance. Existing distribution-shift limitations and qualitative failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that closed-source results came from API calls in May 2025, explicitly documents AIME-24 selection of block size and beam width, and specifies the 8-gram overlap threshold. Training hardware, hyperparameters, decoding settings, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Fu et al., Deep Think with Confidence, contrasting entropy-based guidance with reward-informed value models and suggesting their combination. The remaining related-work positioning is retained; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, the benchmark and main-results passages are locally rewritten, and a related-work paragraph is added. Acknowledgments, conference identification, and appendix references are updated. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is shortened to 2025 columns and fewer model rows, while Table 2 preserves the full comparison. Several main-text plots are redrawn with revised scales, legends, and aggregate curves. Figure 1 adds budget labels and removes the o3-mini reference line; appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves evaluation transparency by separating the primary 2025 aggregate from AIME-24 validation and reporting a contamination check. It also removes the abstract's 45.7%-at-64-generations statement, which conflicts with the tables' N=256 setting. These are useful corrections without substantial new experimental evidence. Readers must still distinguish the two-benchmark main results from the four-benchmark averages retained in Figure 1 and Table 2.
